The T-Rex skeleton has thicker ribs than the velociraptor skeleton. To the left of the T-Rex stand two glass display cases, one containing an ammonite fossil. The number of museum guards in the hall is one more than the number of display cases. One guard, who is older than the other, is standing in front of a display case, looking at a school child. The number of children is twice the number of display cases. The child is shorter than the guard and is holding a toy dinosaur, pointing it at the T-Rex. The older guard is pointing a flashlight's beam at the floor. The velociraptor skeleton has its claw breaking a small display placard on the floor. A large museum banner hangs on the wall behind the T-Rex. The T-Rex's tail extends over one of the display cases.
